correctness.rationale: The shared beta mixture gives P(no positive)=E(1-P)^k=Qk=(beta)_k/(alpha+beta)_k exactly. F_{k+1}/Fk-1 has sign beta+(1-alpha)k, and gamma-ratio asymptotics separate alpha<1,=1,>1; in alpha>1 the global maximum is F_K (possible K,K+1 tie). Direct subtraction gives C_{k+1}-Ck=(Hk-1)/(k(k+1)) for k>=2, Hk=alpha k(k+1)Qk/(alpha+beta+k). H_{k+1}/Hk-1 has sign 2beta+(1-alpha)k, hence at most min and max. For alpha>1, Qk=o(1/k) makes Ck>1 eventually, preventing late declining tail from beating any strict savings. Independent exact Fraction recurrence corroborated H4<1<H5 and H28>1>H29 for (3/2,5/2), C5=10143/10240, and all k<=1000. This is analytical infinite-size proof plus bounded corroboration, not clinical validation.

originality.rationale: Earlier beta-binomial group-testing research derives the negative-pool probability and analyzes costs for bounded cluster sizes or generic optimal partition algorithms; these are acknowledged. The exact all-integer alpha-beta savings phase and at-most-two-turn cost classification, including a genuinely double-turn witness, were not found as implications of inspected theorems. The 2011 correlated-response full text is now available and was inspected, reducing prior access risk.
residual_risks: Novelty is in the shape/boundary classification, not the well-known exact expected-cost formula.
Finite population-size caps, dilution, imperfect tests, and adaptive partitions may change optimality and are outside claim.
Unindexed specialist derivation of the same all-k alpha-beta phase may exist.

value.rationale: Two-stage pooling under shared beta risk is a standard meaningful exchangeable model. An exact criterion for when any uniform pool can save tests, and the surprise that costs may have a local minimum then a local maximum (so unimodal search can mislead), are practically interpretable yet rigorous mathematical phase laws. Finite population and imperfect tests explicitly excluded.
